Title: AKU SONAM- Kenya Alumni Social 2023.
NewsSummary: The AKU SONAM (Aga Khan University School of Nursing and Midwifery) alumni gathered for a vibrant day of networking, fostering connections, and enjoying a fun-filled event.
NewsContent:
​​Our recently launched Bachelor of Science in Nursing (Direct Entry programme) will guide the next cohort of young nurses to not only make an impact, but also encourage more to join us in changing this wonderful vocation. These were the words that were echoed frequently at the AKU SONAM -Kenya Alumni Social that took place on Saturday 24, June 2023 at the Nairobi Serena Hotel. 

The aim of the event was to bring together our esteemed AKU SONAM alumni, reenergize the alumni association, and chart the way forward for the future. The former AKU students got a chance to dance, network and immortalize the day thanks to the photo booth that had been set up at the event venue.

“Scholarships provide an avenue for all to get access to an education. Thanks to the numerous sponsors that have helped us to provide support to our students over the years.” Prof Eunice Ndirangu- Mugo, Dean- SONAM EA stated.

The Dean challenged the alumni in attendance to pool resources together to support needy students as opposed to relying on external support from various corporates because even that can come to an end. The dean pointed out that AKU SONAM’s programmes are transformative and have had an immense impact in the lives of many past students.  "Rose Maina, who is also a member of the AKU SONAM faculty is also a beneficiary of the EN-RN conversion programme which was initially supported by Johnson and Johnson Foundation. We are very grateful for their continuous support over the years,” she added. 

 “AKU is a world-renowned school that offers world class programmes, and we are where we are now because of AKU,” beamed Joel Navwore, an AKU SONAM class of 2022 alumnus.

Joy Makena, class of 2014 also had nothing but praise for the institution. “AKU is a state-of-the-art facility. As students, we were really taken care of, and I am extremely grateful to you (the staff and faculty) for taking care of us and just offering enriching our educational experience.” 

Zeddy Komen, a 2012 alumna, shared that she was dubbed the “Ebola warrior” for her bravery while dealing with the disease during an assignment in Liberia. She credits her education at AKU for preparing her for that moment. “AKU prepared me for my current role as a nurse mentor and international nurse supervisor. I oversee nurses in Sierra Leone, Sudan, and Libya.” During the COVID-19 pandemic she spent two years in Somalia, and thereafter a presidential commendation (Uzalendo Award) on June 1, 2020, for her work there. She also praised the education at AKU for equipping her with skills in public speaking that have be instrumental in her role as mentor.  “Our education not only sets us apart in clinical practice but especially in the field.”

​​AKU SONAM remains steadfast in its efforts to actualize its vision to educate, impact, and transform the next generation of young nurses for global future.
